draft.title: Outputs and customer service
card: Outputs are what an operations process produces for customers. They can be goods, which are physical items, or services, which are actions done for the customer.
the help and care a business gives before, during and after a sale, such as advice, friendly staff and handling complaints.
a promise from the business to repair or replace a faulty good, or fix a problem, within a set time after the sale.
Customers judge the whole package, not only the good or service itself. Poor service or a weak warranty can lower how they rate a business, even when the output is sound.
draft.remember: What the customer gets includes the output plus the service and warranty around it.

a.q: Which of these is a service output rather than a good?
a.why: A haircut is an action done for the customer, so it is a service. The boots, bread and laptop are physical items, so they are goods.
a.clue: Which one is an action, not an item you can carry home?

b.q: Leila buys a washing machine from an appliance store in Parramatta. It works well, but staff ignore her calls when she asks about the repair promise. How is she most likely to judge the business?
opts: Poorly, because after-sale service is part of what she gets
Well, because the machine works so nothing else matters
Well, because a warranty only applies to services
Poorly, because the washing machine is a service output
b.why: Customers judge the output together with the service and warranty around it. Ignoring her calls weakens the after-sale service, which can lower her rating even though the machine works. The idea that only the machine matters is wrong, as the card says customers judge the whole package.
b.clue: Think about what the customer judges beyond the machine itself.

b.best: Poorly, because after-sale service is part of what she gets
